verification.note: Read from the product having one load, which its group 1 controls, as on other one-load products.

steps.text: Plug the lamp or device (the load) you want to control into the outlet on the bottom of the module, with the load's own switch in the on position.
Plug the module into an unswitched wall outlet.
steps.expect: Status LED and the load turn on

steps.text: If the load does not turn on, turn it on with the switch on the load itself.
Tap the SET button to toggle the load on and off.

notes: Do not plug the module into a switched outlet, a filtered power strip or an AC line filter, and do not stack Insteon modules.
The pass-through outlet on the front works as an ordinary uncontrolled outlet; do not plug another home automation product into it.
After installation the load's own switch no longer controls it unless load sensing is enabled.

steps.text: Use the SET button to set the module to the state you want the controller to activate (on or off).
With the controller in linking mode, press and hold the module's SET button for 3 seconds.
steps.expect: Status LED flashes twice and then turns on solid

notes: The module links as a responder: set the controller to linking mode first (for most controllers, press and hold an On or scene button for 10 seconds or the SET button for 3 seconds), then press and hold this module's SET button.
Pressing and holding the SET button for 3 seconds on its own puts the module in linking mode (Status LED blinks) for four minutes; the manual uses this to assign an X10 address.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
With the controller in linking mode, press and hold the module's SET button for 3 seconds.
steps.expect: Status LED flashes twice and then turns on solid

steps.text: Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request; the device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version.
Have the Hub send Ping a few times to check the link.

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder; the device makes no link back to the Hub.

To add the device without its SET button, have the Hub send it Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09, cmd2 0x01; extended for an i2CS device) right after it starts ALL-Linking, in place of the SET button step.
Once linked, the Hub reads the device's settings with Get Operating Flags and an extended Get for group 1.

verification.note: No document describes this; it's how the device is set up in practice.

steps.text: With the controller in unlinking mode, press and hold the module's SET button for 3 seconds.
steps.expect: Status LED flashes twice and then turns on solid

notes: To unlink, set the controller to unlinking mode first (for most controllers, press and hold an On or scene button for 10 seconds twice or the SET button for 3 seconds twice), then press and hold this module's SET button for 3 seconds.

steps.text: Unlink the module from any controller that controls it.
Unplug the module.
Wait about 10 seconds.
While holding down the SET button, plug the module back in without letting go of the button.
Keep holding the SET button for 3 seconds, then release it.
steps.expect: Status LED flashes once and turns off; after a few seconds the Status LED and the load turn on

steps.text: Unlink the module from every controller it is linked to.

notes: The manual says to unlink the module from all controllers before you stop using it; otherwise the controllers keep retrying commands and slow the system.
If an X10 primary address was assigned, remove it as well so the module does not keep responding to X10 commands.

steps.text: Remove the device from every scene on the Hub first.
Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09), as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

notes: The Hub won't remove a device that still belongs to a scene.

verification.note: No document describes this; it's how the device is set up in practice.
